description: On a runner with Docker and systemd: report mode changes nothing and shows the expected-containers list it would create; apply creates the list once, from every container present, marks it not reviewed, and never rewrites it, and installs an enabled prune timer whose script never touches volumes. The prune refuses an age limit under 24 hours, so the tests make their containers and images 30 days old rather than lower it (a container by stopping Docker and editing config.v2.json; an image by loading a docker save archive written by hand, with the date in it). Before the list is reviewed, the prune removes no container and no image. After review, a stopped container that nothing protects is first recorded in /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal (0700 root directory, 0600 file) and left alone; a run inside the grace period leaves it and says until when; a run after it (the record moved back 145 hours) removes it and drops the record. Its age counts from when it stopped: one stopped 29 days ago and one never started, created 30 days ago, are recorded; one created 30 days ago that stopped just now is not (the times are set by stopping Docker and editing config.v2.json). A recorded container added to the list, or started again, loses its record. When the record cannot be written (a read-only bind mount), no container is removed and the exit is 1, through the timer's script and through Prune now; a GRACE_HOURS under 24 written by hand is refused by the prune; an OLDER_THAN_HOURS that is 0, 23, 8761, empty, not a number, quoted or followed by anything is refused too, with nothing at all recorded or removed and exit 1, while 8760 and 24 are used; the settings file is read as text and never run (commands on other lines, a command substitution or an arithmetic subscript as a value: nothing runs, and such a value is refused), and the last line for a name wins; and when the review is withdrawn the prune removes nothing and clears the record. Stopped containers that are on the list, have an unless-stopped policy, or are labelled tc.keep are kept with their images. Images, with a test registry on 127.0.0.1 standing in for a real one: Dangling (and a settings file with no PRUNE_IMAGES) removes the untagged image only; All also removes the tagged image pushed to the registry, printing its repo@sha256 to the journal (and that reference pulls it back), keeps the one built here and says why, and keeps tc.keep; a failing docker image ls removes no image and exits 1. Which store the runner uses decides what All must do: on the classic image store as described; on the containerd image store, where every image has a digest, All keeps every tagged image and says why. The last steps restart Docker on the other store and check All there too, so both stores are covered whichever the runner starts with. The image is pushed to the test registry only on the classic store: on the containerd store it has a repo@sha256 digest without one, and that store's push used HTTPS on Docker 29.4.2 whatever insecure-registries said. Bad input is refused with exit 2 before anything is written. A host without Docker is Tier 2. A container label is untrusted: one whose Compose project label carries a forged row cannot add a row or a field to the container listing, so a reviewed prune keeps the listed stopped container the forged row named, names the containers whose labels cannot be read, keeps them, and never prints the label; a new list leaves them off and says so. When docker ps fails but docker info answers (a shim on PATH), the prune prints ERROR, exits 1 and removes nothing, and does not reach its network or build-cache step; Prune now exits 1; and the list is not created, exit 3. Docker stopped (docker.service stopped, docker.socket still listening, a restart: always container on the list): the prune service has Requisite=docker.service and After=, not Requires=; starting it, by hand or when the timer itself fires, does not start Docker and does not run the prune, and the timer stays active; the prune run by hand prints one line saying Docker is not running, removes nothing and exits 0; the component in Report and in Apply (exit 0: neither needs Docker), in Apply with Prune now (which does not run, exit 3), and with no list (not created, exit 3) leaves docker.service inactive; started again, the timer's service runs the prune normally. A changed service file or prune script is rewritten with a daemon-reload and the timer is not restarted (same ActiveEnterTimestamp and NextElapseUSecRealtime, no prune run); a schedule change restarts it. With no docker.service unit (its file, drop-ins and /etc/init.d/docker moved away), the service is written without the dependency lines and says so, and the unit starts and runs the prune; with the unit back, the next run writes them again. Version 13: the installed prune reads the pending-removal file with the shared tc_pending_lines and has no parser of its own; and a pending-removal file with a comment, a blank line, a malformed line, a CRLF line and a second line for the same container gives what version 12 gave: two unreadable lines counted and dropped, the first line for the container used, nothing removed early, and the file written again clean. Version 14: the installed prune writes pending-removal with tc_state_write, the function in the block marked tc-docker state that the three Docker monitors share (a step reads the installed prune for it). A /var/lib/tc-docker that is not owned by root is not used and not taken over, and a symlink in the record's place is not followed, written through or replaced: either way no container is removed and the prune exits 1; with the record a regular file again, the same prune removes the container whose record is due. The script's opening comment is short and points to the README (a step reads it). Version 15: the daemon.json part is in Docker - Configure Daemon Limits [Lin], with its tests. Here, a step reads the script for what is left of it (nothing: no python3, none of the four input variables); Apply, a job that still passes those four variables (with values version 14 refused), and every other run in this spec leave daemon.json as it was, with no backup and no staging file beside it. Version 16: a REQUIRED_CONTAINERS line left in the settings file by version 2 is not read: with it there and no list, Report mode and Apply list only the containers present, and every entry on the new list is a container on the host.

steps.run:
cat > /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-age <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# tc-test-age NAME=CREATED[,FINISHED] ...: stop Docker, set those containers' Created
# (and State.FinishedAt) in their config.v2.json, start Docker again. Docker sets both
# times itself and has no way to change them, so this is how a test makes a container old.
set -e
declare -A ids
for a in "$@"; do ids[${a%%=*}]=$(docker inspect -f '{{.Id}}' "${a%%=*}"); done
root=$(docker info --format '{{.DockerRootDir}}')
if [ -d /run/systemd/system ]; then systemctl stop docker.socket docker.service; else pkill -x dockerd; while pgrep -x dockerd >/dev/null; do sleep 1; done; fi
for a in "$@"; do
  n=${a%%=*}; v=${a#*=}; c=${v%%,*}; f="$root/containers/${ids[$n]}/config.v2.json"
  if [ "$v" != "$c" ]; then jq --arg c "$c" --arg f "${v#*,}" '.Created=$c | .State.FinishedAt=$f' "$f" > "$f.tc"
  else jq --arg c "$c" '.Created=$c' "$f" > "$f.tc"; fi
  mv "$f.tc" "$f"
done
if [ -d /run/systemd/system ]; then systemctl start docker.service; else (setsid dockerd >/var/log/tc-test-dockerd.log 2>&1 </dev/null &); fi
for i in $(seq 30); do docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; done
for a in "$@"; do docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} created {{.Created}}, finished {{.State.FinishedAt}}' "${a%%=*}"; done
EOF

cat > /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-old-image <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# tc-test-old-image LABEL [TAG]: load an image, built here, whose build time (Created) is
# 30 days ago; labelled LABEL (key=value) and tc.nonce; tagged TAG, or untagged. Prints
# its id. docker import and docker build stamp an image with the time now, and the prune
# never removes an image younger than OLDER_THAN_HOURS (24 at the least), so this is how
# a test makes an old one: a docker save archive written by hand, with the date in it.
set -e
label=$1; tag=${2:-}
w=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$w"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$w/root/bin"; cp /bin/true "$w/root/bin/"
tar -C "$w/root" -cf "$w/layer.tar" .
c=$(date -u -d '30 days ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
jq -cn --arg c "$c" --arg a "$(docker version --format '{{.Server.Arch}}')" --arg d "sha256:$(sha256sum "$w/layer.tar" | cut -d' ' -f1)" --arg n "$(date +%s%N)" --arg k "${label%%=*}" --arg v "${label#*=}" '{architecture:$a,os:"linux",created:$c,config:{Labels:{"tc.nonce":$n,($k):$v}},rootfs:{type:"layers",diff_ids:[$d]},history:[{created:$c,created_by:"tc-test"}]}' > "$w/config.json"
cfg=$(sha256sum "$w/config.json" | cut -d' ' -f1); mv "$w/config.json" "$w/$cfg.json"
jq -cn --arg cfg "$cfg.json" --arg t "$tag" '[{Config:$cfg,RepoTags:(if $t == "" then null else [$t] end),Layers:["layer.tar"]}]' > "$w/manifest.json"
tar -C "$w" -cf "$w/image.tar" manifest.json "$cfg.json" layer.tar
out=$(docker load -i "$w/image.tar")
if [ -n "$tag" ]; then docker image inspect -f '{{.Id}}' "$tag"; else printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^Loaded image ID: //p' | grep .; fi
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# tc-test-registry PORT DIR [CERT KEY]: a minimal image registry (the Docker
# Registry HTTP API v2, enough for docker push, docker pull and a manifest
# lookup) on 127.0.0.1, so a test can give an image a real registry digest
# without the internet. With CERT and KEY it serves HTTPS. Files in DIR change
# how it answers, so a test can switch them on and off:
#   htpasswd   "user:password": every request needs that Basic login
#   ratelimit  manifest requests get 429 Too Many Requests, as Docker Hub's do
#   delay      manifest requests wait this many seconds first
# Every manifest request is appended to DIR/requests.log.
import base64, hashlib, os, ssl, sys, time, uuid
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from urllib.parse import urlparse, parse_qs
PORT, DIR = int(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2]
for sub in ("blobs", "uploads", "manifests"):
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(DIR, sub), exist_ok=True)
def safe(s): return s.replace("/", "_").replace(":", "_")
def sha(b): return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()
def flag(n):
    try: return open(os.path.join(DIR, n)).read().strip()
    except OSError: return None
class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
    def send(self, code, body=b"", headers=None):
        self.send_response(code)
        for k, v in (headers or {}).items(): self.send_header(k, v)
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.send_header("Docker-Distribution-API-Version", "registry/2.0")
        self.end_headers()
        if self.command != "HEAD": self.wfile.write(body)
    def body(self):
        n = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
        if n: return self.rfile.read(n)
        if self.headers.get("Transfer-Encoding", "").lower() != "chunked": return b""
        out = b""
        while True:
            size = int(self.rfile.readline().strip().split(b";")[0], 16)
            if size == 0: self.rfile.readline(); return out
            out += self.rfile.read(size); self.rfile.readline()
    def route(self):
        u = urlparse(self.path); p = u.path; q = parse_qs(u.query)
        login = flag("htpasswd")
        if login:
            want = "Basic " + base64.b64encode(login.encode()).decode()
            if self.headers.get("Authorization") != want:
                self.body()
                return self.send(401, b'{"errors":[{"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"authentication required"}]}',
                                 {"WWW-Authenticate": 'Basic realm="tc-test-registry"', "Content-Type": "application/json"})
        if p in ("/v2", "/v2/"): return self.send(200, b"{}")
        if "/blobs/uploads/" in p:
            name, rest = p[4:].split("/blobs/uploads/", 1)
            if self.command == "POST":
                uid = uuid.uuid4().hex
                open(f"{DIR}/uploads/{uid}", "wb").close()
                return self.send(202, headers={"Location": f"/v2/{name}/blobs/uploads/{uid}", "Range": "0-0", "Docker-Upload-UUID": uid})
            uid = rest.strip("/"); f = f"{DIR}/uploads/{uid}"
            with open(f, "ab") as fh: fh.write(self.body())
            if self.command == "PATCH":
                return self.send(202, headers={"Location": f"/v2/{name}/blobs/uploads/{uid}", "Range": f"0-{max(os.path.getsize(f) - 1, 0)}", "Docker-Upload-UUID": uid})
            d = q["digest"][0]
            if sha(open(f, "rb").read()) != d: return self.send(400, b'{"errors":[{"code":"DIGEST_INVALID"}]}')
            os.replace(f, f"{DIR}/blobs/{safe(d)}")
            return self.send(201, headers={"Location": f"/v2/{name}/blobs/{d}", "Docker-Content-Digest": d})
        if "/blobs/" in p:
            d = p.rsplit("/blobs/", 1)[1]; f = f"{DIR}/blobs/{safe(d)}"
            if not os.path.exists(f): return self.send(404, b'{"errors":[{"code":"BLOB_UNKNOWN"}]}')
            return self.send(200, open(f, "rb").read(), {"Docker-Content-Digest": d, "Content-Type": "application/octet-stream"})
        if "/manifests/" in p:
            name, ref = p[4:].rsplit("/manifests/", 1)
            if self.command == "PUT":
                data = self.body(); d = sha(data)
                for r in (ref, d):
                    open(f"{DIR}/manifests/{safe(name)}@{safe(r)}", "wb").write(data)
                    open(f"{DIR}/manifests/{safe(name)}@{safe(r)}.type", "w").write(self.headers.get("Content-Type", ""))
                return self.send(201, headers={"Location": f"/v2/{name}/manifests/{d}", "Docker-Content-Digest": d})
            with open(f"{DIR}/requests.log", "a") as log: log.write(f"{self.command} {p}\n")
            delay = flag("delay")
            if delay: time.sleep(int(delay))
            if flag("ratelimit") is not None:
                return self.send(429, b'{"errors":[{"code":"TOOMANYREQUESTS","message":"You have reached your pull rate limit."}]}', {"Content-Type": "application/json"})
            f = f"{DIR}/manifests/{safe(name)}@{safe(ref)}"
            if not os.path.exists(f): return self.send(404, b'{"errors":[{"code":"MANIFEST_UNKNOWN","message":"manifest unknown"}]}', {"Content-Type": "application/json"})
            data = open(f, "rb").read()
            return self.send(200, data, {"Docker-Content-Digest": sha(data), "Content-Type": open(f + ".type").read()})
        return self.send(404)
    do_GET = do_HEAD = do_POST = do_PATCH = do_PUT = route
srv = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", PORT), H)
if len(sys.argv) > 4:
    ctx = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER); ctx.load_cert_chain(sys.argv[3], sys.argv[4])
    srv.socket = ctx.wrap_socket(srv.socket, server_side=True)
srv.serve_forever()
EOF

outputContains: tc-registry.test:5055/tc-test-pulled:1 - its registry has it, pull again: tc-registry.test:5055/tc-test-pulled@sha256:

steps.label: The other image store: clean up - daemon.json as it was, Docker restarted, the registry stopped, the test CA and name gone
steps.run: if [ -e /tmp/tc-store-daemon.json ]; then cp -p /tmp/tc-store-daemon.json /etc/docker/daemon.json; else rm -f /etc/docker/daemon.json; fi; rm -f /tmp/tc-store-daemon.json; tc-test-images registry stop; rm -rf /tmp/tc-test-registry /tmp/tc-test-registry.pid /etc/tc-test-pki /etc/docker/certs.d/tc-registry.test:5055; rmdir /etc/docker/certs.d 2>/dev/null; rm -f /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/tc-test-ca.crt; update-ca-certificates --fresh >/dev/null 2>&1; sed -i '/ tc-registry.test$/d' /etc/hosts; grep -c tc-registry.test /etc/hosts || echo 'test name gone'; systemctl restart docker.service && docker info --format 'docker up again: {{.ServerVersion}}'

steps.label: At the end: daemon.json is as it was before the first run of the component (the image-store steps changed it themselves and put it back), with no backup and no staging file
steps.run: { cmp -s /tmp/tc-before.json /etc/docker/daemon.json || { test ! -s /etc/docker/daemon.json && test "$(cat /tmp/tc-before.json)" = '{}'; }; } && echo 'daemon.json as it was'; test -z "$(ls -A /etc/docker | grep -E '^(daemon\.json\.tc-bak-|\.daemon\.json\.tc-)' || true)" && echo 'no backup or staging file'; ls -A /etc/docker; rm -f /tmp/tc-before.json
